title: feat(auth): add --client-id flag to glab auth login
description:
## Description

On self-managed and Dedicated GitLab instances, users authenticating with OAuth currently have to configure `client_id` with `glab config set client_id <id> --host <host>` before logging in, or respond to an interactive paste prompt. Passing a one-off `GITLAB_CLIENT_ID` environment variable is not persisted, which causes subsequent token refreshes to fail once the variable is unset.

This MR adds a `--client-id` flag to `glab auth login`. It allows users and setup scripts to supply the OAuth application client ID in a single command, such as:

```shell
glab auth login --hostname gitlab.example.com --client-id <CLIENT_ID> --web
```

Decisions:
1. When `--client-id` is provided on a self-managed instance, it takes precedence over `GITLAB_CLIENT_ID` and saved config. It is saved to the host configuration together with OAuth tokens when authentication succeeds.
2. If authentication fails, `--client-id` is not saved to disk and existing credentials remain untouched.
3. Passing an empty or whitespace `--client-id` flag is rejected with an error rather than falling back to defaults.
4. `--client-id` is rejected with an error if used against `gitlab.com`, which uses a fixed built-in application ID.
5. `--client-id` is marked mutually exclusive with `--token`, `--stdin`, and `--job-token`. In interactive mode, the token option is omitted from the sign-in menu when `--client-id` is passed.

## Related Issues

Closes #8699

## How has this been tested?

I added unit tests in `internal/commands/auth/login/login_test.go` covering:
- Flag parsing and mutual exclusivity with token flags.
- Rejection of empty or whitespace values for `--client-id`.
- Rejection on `gitlab.com` in both non-interactive and interactive flows.
- Omission of the token option from the interactive sign-in menu.
- Successful device flow persisting both `client_id` and OAuth tokens to disk.
- Failed device flow leaving disk configuration and existing credentials untouched.

The rest runs in the pipeline.

Implemented with AI assistance; I reviewed and tested the changes.

title: docs(work-items): add tester guide for the experimental REST get command
description:
Related to #8586.

Adds `docs/work_items_experimental_tester_guide.md`, a tester guide for the experimental work items REST mode on this branch. It covers:

- What exists today: `glab work-items get <iid>` in REST mode.
- Getting access: the `work_item_rest_api` feature flag, building glab from this branch, and turning on REST mode with `GLAB_WORK_ITEMS_API_MODE` or the `work_items_api_mode` config key.
- Example commands with sample text and JSON output, and the exact error messages for REST mode off and for a missing work item or disabled flag.
- Cases worth trying, known limitations, and where to report problems.

The guide sits in `docs/` outside the generated docs, as the issue suggests. It targets this feature branch so it lands with the command it documents; happy to retarget to `main` if you prefer.

Verified: `markdownlint-cli2` with the project config reports 0 issues.

One checklist item from #8586 is not in this MR: linking the guide from the two epics needs a maintainer, since I cannot edit group epics.

title: feat(milestone): add --include-descendants to milestone list
description:
## Description

Running `glab milestone list --group` only listed milestones defined directly on that group.
There was no way to view milestones from subgroups or descendant projects.

I added the `--include-descendants` flag to `glab milestone list`.
When used with `--group`, glab now fetches milestones from all subgroups and descendant projects.

Because results can now span multiple namespaces, I added an Owner column to the table output when `--include-descendants` is enabled.
This column helps users see which subgroup or project owns each milestone.

A few decisions on the behavior:
1. `--include-descendants` is mutually exclusive with `--project`. Project milestones do not have descendants, so combining them returns an error.
2. The Owner column appears only when `--include-descendants` is set. Standard group and project listings keep their original table format.
3. The Owner column shows the subgroup or project path from the milestone web URL. It falls back to `group/<id>` or `project/<id>` if the URL is unavailable.
4. JSON output includes `group_id` and `project_id` fields for scripting.

## Related Issues

Closes #8709

## How has this been tested?

I tested the mutual exclusivity check by hand using a built `glab` binary:

```shell
$ glab milestone list --project 123 --include-descendants
   ERROR  
  if any flags in the group [project include-descendants] are set none of the 
  others can be; [include-descendants project] were all set.                  
```

I added unit tests covering flag wiring, mock verification for `IncludeDescendents`, table output with the Owner column, and `--show-id`.
I also added tests for mutual exclusivity with `--project`, JSON output, and milestone owner parsing edge cases.

Checks I ran locally on the changed package:

```shell
$ go test -count=1 ./internal/commands/milestone/list/...
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/milestone/list	0.023s
```

```shell
$ go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0 internal/commands/milestone/list/list.go internal/commands/milestone/list/list_test.go
# 0 findings across 2 files
```

I also regenerated the command documentation with `make gen-docs`.

The rest runs in the pipeline.

Implemented with AI assistance; I reviewed and tested the changes.

title: Draft: feat(auth): show one-click verification link and add --open-browser flag to device login
description:
## What this changes

Two improvements to signing in with `glab auth login --device`, so the device flow is faster and less error-prone, especially in environments like GitLab Workspaces where terminal links are clickable.

### A clickable link that already includes your code

Today the device flow asks you to copy a one-time code and then separately open a verification URL and type that code in by hand:

```
First copy your one-time code: L20016PN
Then open this URL on any device to authorize: https://gitlab.com/oauth/device
```

Now, when the GitLab server provides it, the URL shown already has the code filled in (`https://gitlab.com/oauth/device?user_code=L20016PN`). In terminals where links are clickable, you click once and land on a page that is ready to approve, with no copying required. The plain one-time code is still shown for terminals where the link is not clickable, and the flow falls back to the plain URL if the server does not return the pre-filled form.

### Optionally open the browser for you

A new opt-in `--open-browser` flag lets `glab` open the verification URL automatically instead of making you do it:

```shell
glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com --device --open-browser
```

It uses your configured browser (the `$BROWSER` environment variable or the `browser` config setting) and opens the pre-filled URL so the code is already entered. If opening the browser fails, you are told to open the URL manually. The flag is off by default, so nothing changes for headless setups that rely on copy/paste. It only affects the device flow; the `--web` login already opens a browser.

## Related issues

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8337
Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8338

Follow-up to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3234.

## Implementation notes

- `internal/oauth2/device.go`: `StartDeviceFlow` gains an `openBrowser bool` parameter, prefers `VerificationURIComplete` over `VerificationURI` (RFC 8628 §3.3 makes the complete form optional), and calls `utils.OpenInBrowser` when requested.
- `internal/commands/auth/login/login.go`: new `--open-browser` flag on `LoginOptions`, passed through to `StartDeviceFlow`.
- `docs/source/auth/login.md`: regenerated with `make gen-docs`.

## Testing

- `internal/oauth2/device_test.go`: new `httptest` TLS server stub for the device authorization and token endpoints; tests cover showing the pre-filled URL when the server returns it and falling back to the plain URL when it does not.
- `internal/commands/auth/login/login_test.go`: new cases assert `--open-browser` parses to `true` and defaults to `false`.
- `make build`, `go vet`, and the affected test packages pass locally.
